thread.title: Plan would overhaul Ft. Getty RV park
thread.title_full: Plan would overhaul Ft. Getty RV park

author: ohtadmin
title: Plan would overhaul Ft. Getty RV park
text:
The evolution of governing short-term rentals in single-family homes has momentarily plateaued after nearly 15 years of debate at the highest levels of local government.
The consideration of another form of short-term rentals, however, is just beginning.
Bill Salmons, who serves on the hoc committee charged with exploring the future of Fort Getty, is proposing for eight of the 75 seasonal RV sites at Fort Getty to be converted into weekly rentals starting in 2027. Priority would be given to Jamestown residents and their guests. He presented the plan to his colleagues at their April 7 meeting.
Salmons said he was inspired by comments from homeowners who said they wanted to invite family and friends to Jamestown but didn’t have the room in their houses to accommodate them. The plan also includes instituting a lottery to determine who rents the seasonal sites.
“Our objective should be to provide the greatest benefit to the greatest number of people,” he said.
Salmons’ proposal would keep the 2026 season status quo. In ’27, however, 50 seasonal sites would be upgraded with terracing and 50-amp electrical pedestals. The rate would increase to $7,000 that year and 2026 campers would be allowed to renew for the season. If there are more than 50 campers who renew, they would be relegated to the 17 unimproved sites.
In 2028, renewals of the 50 upgraded sites only would be permitted to Jamestown residents. The 2027 renters and people on the waitlist would then enter a lottery to determine who gets whatever is left of those 50 spaces for $8,000. Salmons also suggested staggering the lottery by having one-third of seasonal sites enter the lottery annually.
The current annual fee is $5,750 for residents and $6,250 for out-of-towners. Salmons did not say whether there would continue to be a residential discount for the seasonal sites.
The trailer park by ’28 would now comprise 50 seasonal sites and eight short-term rentals with the remaining 17 unimproved sites being eliminated for green space.
“The lottery will open up the RV camping experience at Fort Getty to a much greater number of people, who are currently precluded from camping here,” he said. “A number of survey respondents supported RV camping because of the diversity it brings to the Jamestown community. A lottery will broaden such diversity, and new campers will enthusiastically explore all that Jamestown has to offer.”
Salmons suggested for lottery winners to maintain their sites for three years.
“It should not be indefinite,” he said.
Salmons said the lottery “broadens the opportunity to others” with about 1,900 RVs registered in Rhode Island.
Member John Potter said he was “generally supportive” of “trying to increase the amount of churn modestly.”
“It’d be nice to create more churn,” he said. “I’m not sure you actually need the lottery for it, but it’s an elegant idea.” Member Richard Smith said he was concerned about the traffic. “Neighbors already complained a little bit about traffic,” he said. “If you were having RVs going in every two weeks or 10 days, I think that would upset the neighbors a little more than the campers” arriving in May and departing in October.
Smith also was concerned about disrupting the “continuity of the park” due to campers becoming familiar with their neighbors.
“There’s less trouble,” he said. “People govern themselves. There’s a lot of unity.” The committee’s chairman, Marisa Quinn, agreed with Smith.
“I think there is something about the community of campers who are up there,” she said. “The community they have amongst each other, and also the spirit and the dedication to Jamestown that they have developed over time.”
“I’ll just clarify my position on this,” Potter added. “People are accustomed to having an undefined tenure and I think we should probably define it. It doesn’t have to be really short. It probably ought not be really long so that we can encourage greater diversity in the population out there without destroying the sense of community that exists. I think we’re just trying to find a balance.”
summary: Salmons said he was inspired by comments from homeowners who said they wanted to invite family and friends to Jamestown but didn’t have the room in their houses to accommodate them. “A number of survey respondents supported RV camping because of the diversity it brings to the Jamestown community. “If you were having RVs going in every two weeks or 10 days, I think that would upset the neighbors a little more than the campers” arriving in May and departing in October.
